newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian Commodities Roundup - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian Commodities Roundup - Nov 19.

text.p: Copper prices raced to a five month peak early in the day before profit taking pared its gains, while nickel prices tumbled to a two year low.
Traders said rising stocks and fund liquidation sent nickel plunging six percent to $6,620 a tonne, down $450 from Friday's finish. This is the lowest level since October 1994.
Subtantial tonnages of Russian nickel had arrived in Europe earlier this year and held off the LME in Rotterdam.
But as prices started to come down some traders decided to cut their losses by delivering the metal into LME warehouses, pushing up LME stocks in the process, traders said.
LME nickel inventories now stand at 44,508 tonnes, the highest since January.
An overhang of stainless steel scrap, an alternative source of nickel preferred by some steel mills, also weighed on values. Two thirds of the world's nickel is used in stainless steel.
Benchmark three month futures at one stage hit $6,600, but a late bout of buying emerged to lift prices slightly to $6,620, still well down on Friday's $7,050 close.
Some traders said further losses were likely in the short term, and first major support was pegged at $6,330.
Three-months copper moved in the opposite direction early in the day to a peak of $2,198, the highest level for five months.
Copper's earlier surge to near key resistance at $2,200 eased back under profit-taking and general liquidation. It closed at $2,159, up $11 from Friday.
Other base metals ended slightly weaker in sluggish trade.

New York precious metals futures end lower Monday on moderate volumes as the complex continued to drift back from the three-week highs seen last week. COMEX December gold ended down $1.40 an ounce at $379.70, after trading in a $381.50-379.40 range. Spot gold in the bullion market closed quoted $378.80/379.30, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $379.10 and the New York close Friday around $380.05/380.55.

NYMEX crude prices ended off Monday after the restart of gasoline making units and lower gas oil futures in London conspired to push refined product prices lower, traders said. December gasoline ended down 1.15 cents a gallon at 65.77 cents. December heat settled off 0.76 cent a gallon at 71.85 cents while December crude ended down 29 cents at $23.88 a barrel.

CBOT wheat futures closed lower on news Egypt bought wheat from Australia, Argentina and France rather than the United States, traders said. Egypt over the weekend bought 600,000 tonnes of wheat with 200,000 coming from Australia, 250,000 from Argentina and 150,000 from France, Cairo trade sources said. Some said it was not a surprise Egypt bypassed the U.S. and noted Friday's sharp break in KCBT and MGE wheat was linked to expectations that Egypt would not buy U.S. supplies. The December contract early in the session dropped below first support at $3.94 per bushel and reached a session low of $3.91 but rebounded late to that first chart plateau at $3.94. Wheat futures closed 3-1/4 to six cents per bushel lower, with December down 3-1/4 at $3.94.

White sugar futures trading remained subdued up to the close with traders still looking for fresh fundamental news to shake the market from its tight trading range. The March contract ended at $303.10 a tonne, up $0.90 from Friday, with other positions mixed. Turnover was 1,218 lots.
